newsitem.title: USA: Kansas governor proposes $112 mln tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Kansas governor proposes $112 mln tax cut.

text.p: Kansas Gov. Bill Graves proposed a $112 million tax cut package as part of his fiscal 1998 budget plan.
In a speech to the legislature Monday evening, Graves said he was presenting "a responsible budget, responsive initiatives and a reduction of tax dollars collected" in his state.
He unveiled a $3.75 billion general fund budget, just 2.4 percent more than the current budget of $3.58 billion.

Graves called for more than $112 million in tax cuts in the coming fiscal year that included eliminating a premiums tax on annuities, income tax credits for commercial and industrial property taxes on machinery and equipment and for adoptions, expanding homestead property tax rebates, repealing the sales tax on remodeling, and reducing the income tax rates for single residents.
In addition, Graves proposed a two-year 30 percent reduction in the uniform school finance levy.

His budget includes nearly $20 million to more quickly address an inequity in the school finance formula. The proposed spending plan also provides $12 million to increase per pupil funding by $22 to $3,670.
Graves also vowed to protect the state's 7.5 percent ending balance that is required by law.

"To speculate on the economic security of this state by spending dollars that do not exist is inappropriate," the governor said in his speech. "There is no Kansas charge card. Speculation about the future is neither cause to abandon conservative economic principles, nor cause for an unwarranted reduction in the state's protection against economic calamity -- the 7.5 percent ending balance."
